summary: Recommends what information a site should publish for each service it offers over the ARPANET. There are two kinds: details programmers need to connect to the service, and details a user needs to use it. Together these form a functional document, as described in RFC 115.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 118 recommends that each network service document both the technical details needed to connect and the instructions users need to use it. It also describes how the Network Information Center would distribute and maintain those documents.

subtitle: Recommendations for documenting services available to network users.

tldr.problem: Programmers and users at other sites need information to connect to a network facility and use it.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC recommends a functional document with technical connection details, user instructions and any differences for network users.
tldr.outcome: The Network Information Center is to distribute and maintain copies of each functional document in its station collections.

sections.title: Two Kinds of Information
sections.content:
Each service made available over the network needs information for system programmers and for users. Programmers need details for establishing a connection, such as socket numbers, message formats and character-set information.

Users need information on how to access and use the service. These two kinds of information form a functional document, as described in RFC 115.
sections.plainLanguage: Programmers need connection details, while users need instructions for using the service. The RFC says both belong in a functional document.

sections.title: Explain Network-Specific User Differences
sections.content:
User information can cover features unique to network users, features shared with users at the service site, and details unique to a particular user site. The user site prepares its own local information from details supplied by the service site.

At first, the service site may add a short network-user document to its existing manuals. It can explain differences in login or control-card sequences, echo behavior, syntax or available features. If network use has no special differences, the document should say so explicitly. It should also tell users how to get help.
sections.plainLanguage: Documentation should explain what changes for someone connecting over the network. If nothing changes, the document should say that clearly and tell users where to ask for help.

sections.title: Distribution Through the NIC
sections.content:
The Network Information Center plans to distribute and maintain one copy of each facility's functional document in each Network Station NIC Collection. The RFC asks service sites to send 100 copies of each manual and its updates to the NIC.

Users may obtain documentation from the service site or copy it from their local NIC Collection. Each facility's information should include an address and any price for obtaining additional copies.
sections.plainLanguage: The NIC would keep a copy of each service document in station collections. Users could get a copy from the service site or their local collection.
